intro.author: John (1:1, 4, 9), writing from the island of Patmos. Traditionally the apostle John; since early centuries some, noting differences in style from John's Gospel, have suggested a different John.
intro.written: Traditionally about AD 95, late in the reign of Emperor Domitian; some scholars date it to the late 60s, after Nero's persecution
intro.audience: Seven churches in the Roman province of Asia, in what is now western Turkey (1:11)
intro.setting: John was on Patmos, a small island off the coast of Asia Minor, 'for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus' (1:9). The churches faced pressure to honor the emperor and the gods of local trade guilds, hostility from neighbors, and the temptations of comfort and compromise. Revelation is an 'apocalypse' (an unveiling), a prophecy and a letter at once, full of symbols drawn from Daniel, Ezekiel, Isaiah, Zechariah and Exodus. Christians read its visions in different ways: as about the first-century world, as unfolding church history, as future events, or as timeless pictures of the struggle between God and evil.
intro.purpose: To encourage believers to stay faithful under pressure, to warn against compromise, and to show that God and the Lamb reign and will finally defeat evil and make all things new.
intro.bigIdea: Jesus, the slain and risen Lamb, reigns now and will defeat evil and make all things new.
